Semantic Environmental Trajectories of Territories

Website

docs.title: About
docs.text:
Human activities are the main drivers of the observed environmental megatrends such as climate change, biodiversity loss, use of resources, pollutions, …, which impact territories at all scales. Better study and understand the environmental trajectory of a territory, by selecting and using relevant, available, and comparable over time and space indicators, can help to master these megatrends, which appears as one of the main challenges regarding the sustainability of humankind. In this context, the TRACES project will adopt an Artificial Intelligence (AI) approach in order to define, model, implement, enrich, interrogate, analyze, forecast and visualize the environmental trajectory of a territory. To achieve such a complete processing chain, the TRACES project will rely on three domains of AI, Knowledge Representation, Machine Learning and Multi-Agent Systems.

Our first research hypothesis is that the semantic approach supported in Knowledge Representation through ontological models and languages, and Knowledge Graphs (KG) formalism and tools, can help, not only to build and implement semantic environmental trajectories of territories (SETT), but also to enrich them with complementary knowledge relying on the Linked (Open) Data available on the Web. Second, Machine Learning offer valuable techniques, algorithms and tools to group and categorize similar SETT in clusters, but also to extract frequent patterns in these SETT and then to complete then for forecasting future SETT. The third research hypothesis we make is that a Multi-Agent System approach helps to better understand the factors that draw territories trajectories, by modeling and simulating the way territories evolve and behave under systemic constraints. We will consider here that an environmental trajectory can be defined on the basis of a set of environmental indicators, built themselves using official data collected from surveys, various physical sensors, satellite images, etc. The environmental trajectory object produced and analyzed by the TRACES project will thus give an account of the dynamics of the studied territory, and in particular, convey its evolution in terms of biodiversity, nature conservation and resilience to climate change.

The models, algorithms, KG and agents designed by the TRACES project will contribute to a better exploration of environmental trajectories of territories as objects of study. Thus, the proposed processing chain is intended to assist professionals and experts in spatial planning in their longitudinal and comparative analyses, decision-makers in the elaboration of future environmental policies at different territorial levels, but also citizens in their understanding of the public policies implemented and the evolution of the territories they live in.

The first scientific and technical challenge for the TRACES project concerns the modeling of environmental trajectory of territory, which to the best of our knowledge, constitutes the first attempt for representing this notion by adopting a Semantic Web-based approach. The difficulty lies in both the definition of such an environmental trajectory in terms of indicators of possibly different kinds and their measures, and in the coupling with its intrinsic spatial and temporal dimensions. Therefore, as a whole, an environmental trajectory of a territory appears as a complex multidimensional and multigranular object whose modelling, visualization and analysis are difficult and yet unexplored tasks. An ontological model for such an object should also include standard vocabularies in order to facilitate data integration and ensure the reusability of the KG representing the SETT that will be created from both this conceptual description and the values of the indicators Exploring how Machine Learning clustering techniques can be applied to SETT faces three main challenges: 1) providing similarity measures adapted to the representations of multimodal data evolving along the temporal axis; 2) enabling multimodal clustering of trajectories for the definition of trajectory profiles; 3) enabling temporal prediction over multimodal data representations.

The main challenges raised by modeling environmental trajectories using an executable multi-agent system lie in: 1) leveraging SETT to derive, possibly in an automated manner, multi-agent based models reproducing past environmental trajectories; 2) combining and visualizing in the same hybrid models, spatially-explicit agents modeling human behavior and lattice-based territorial changes; 3) exploiting a series of scenarios highlighting relevant policies to provide useful prescriptive analysis. Lastly, several definitions of an environmental trajectory will be proposed to handle different perspectives on this study object. Indicators and data will be provided and elaborated by partner ISE, using the Swiss Data Cube platform. Taking advantage of the fact that TRACES is a joint project between Swiss and French researchers, we will choose three types of territory to conduct longitudinal and comparative analysis: 1) Swiss territories (at the state, canton and commune levels); 2) French territories (at the department, commune and metropolitan levels); 3) on both sides of the French-Swiss border (at commune and metropolitan levels). However, our approach intends to be generic and applicable to worldwide territories.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The WiDOP project is a collaboration with the i3mainz applied research institute, aiming at the automatic detection of objects in a 3D point cloud based on business knowledge. This partnership project, involving Deutsche Bahn, Fraport (Frankfurt Airport) and Metronom, a Deutsche Bahn subcontractor, aims to improve the business process of detecting objects close to the railway. The business processes of DB and Fraport differ because their contexts differ. However, the time spent manually searching for objects in the scene is the common problem of both trades.

This project is a collaboration between two teams of the Le2i laboratory. The first is the SISI team (Information Systems, Image Systems), whose members take part in the CheckSem project for knowledge processing. The second is the SINC team (Non-Conventional Imaging Systems) in Auxerre, for signal processing. The WiDOP project thus gives business processes a 3D semantic and topological analysis method that automates processing across all 3D objects in a 3D point cloud. This makes it possible to define tasks answering 3D topological questions, or topological inference, by modelling knowledge about operational topological analysis processes. To do so, new elements called topological "built-ins", used in SWRL logic programs, were designed and developed to define topological rules between geometric elements. The rule below looks for a "Mast" (electric pole) at a distance of 50 m from another "Mast" and whose particular feature is to be vertical. In that case, this object is also a "Mast". The figures below show the first results of object detection in a point cloud. Detection is represented by a bounding box whose colour indicates its semantic nature.

docs.title: Research
docs.text:
My research lies at the intersection of knowledge modelling, generative AI and agentic systems. The central goal is to design intelligent architectures able to reason, adapt and interact with humans in a natural, context-aware way.

  • Generative AI and LLMs
  • Hybrid neuro-symbolic AI
  • RAG and knowledge graphs
  • AI agents and human-machine interaction
  • Cognitive Network Science

docs.title: Generative AI and large language models
docs.text:
The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has profoundly transformed natural language processing. I am particularly interested in their use in demanding business settings: extractive and abstractive summarisation, multi-label classification, Dynamic Topic Modeling, and economic and strategic intelligence.

This work was carried out with the company Actualis until 2022. It continues with the TIL Laboratory at the University of Burgundy, notably on semantic frames and on formalising idiomaticity as lexico-grammatical patterns.

Business information extraction tasks from text. Source: Arslan, Munawar, Cruz, Journal of Decision Systems, 2024, CC BY 4.0 licence.

docs.title: Hybrid neuro-symbolic AI
docs.text:
Given the known limitations of LLMs (hallucinations, incompleteness, lack of traceability), I develop hybrid neuro-symbolic approaches that combine knowledge graphs and generative models. These architectures extract structured knowledge from text and return a reliable, explainable representation of it.

This work began with the DL4Graphs project with the company DAVI (France Relance funding) and was extended by a European OCRE Google Cloud project (€250k of cloud credit, 2022) using infrastructure such as Vertex AI, Neo4J and Kubernetes.

Neuro-symbolic AI combines the strengths of symbolic and neural AI. Source: Bougzime et al., Materials & Design, 2025, CC BY 4.0 licence.

Propose, then judge (2026). In a conversational assistant, inexpensive extractors propose candidate values, and a small calibrated decision model picks one of them or abstains, then acts, ignores or asks the user. This judge, with fewer than half a billion parameters, is more accurate than LLMs with 27 to 180 billion parameters. The multilingual model laya-slotjudge-m46 (46 languages) is open. docs.title: RAG and knowledge graphs
docs.text:
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is today one of the most promising paradigms for grounding LLMs in reliable, evolving knowledge bases. My approach uses knowledge graphs to structure, enrich and validate the knowledge base available to the model, which allows more precise navigation, better extraction of implicit relations and more relevant answers.

This work is explored in particular in Oualid Bougzime's PhD on knowledge management for smart materials and 4D printing.

docs.title: AI agents and human-machine interaction
docs.text:
My most recent research focuses on agentic AI: systems able to perceive their environment, reason, plan and act autonomously to achieve complex goals.

This work takes place mainly within the LabCom LAMAE (ANR-24-LCV1-0008-01), a joint laboratory with the company DAVI The Humanizers, dedicated to developing multimodal, empathetic and adaptive agents. The ambition is to design agents that do not merely answer, but perceive, understand and adapt to each user, based on a 4M architecture:

Dimension Description Multi-Agents Expert, emotional and contextual agents collaborating in a network Multi-Graph-RAG Distributed memory and structured knowledge storage Multi-Modality Processing of text, image, sound and video Multi-Profile Dynamic adaptation to user profiles and needs

Two recent results illustrate this topic. LAMAE-Mem (ISCS 2026) proposes a three-tier memory architecture (working, episodic and long-term) for LLM agents that take emotions into account. A study presented at AGENTICS 2026 analyses how hallucinations propagate between agents across five multi-agent architectures. It received the Best Paper Award.

CoA-Text2OWL framework: a chain of agents builds an ontology from text. Source: Jabbar, Cruz, report, 2025.

docs.title: Cognitive Network Science for human-AI systems
docs.text:
Cognitive Network Science applies graph theory and complexity science to model human cognitive structures, such as semantic memory or emotional associations. I use it to understand and improve interactions between humans and AI.

A systematic review, presented at KES 2026 and following the PRISMA 2020 method, identifies five themes: theoretical foundations, auditing AI and LLM systems, human-AI collective intelligence, social and emotional AI, and education, creativity and cognitive augmentation.

The five themes of the systematic review. Source: review GitHub repository, CC BY 4.0 licence.

A second line of work focuses on cognitive load and metacognition in human-AI conversations. It proposes a formal framework that estimates both directly from transcripts, without sensors. Conversations are represented as a multiplex temporal network whose layers capture semantic, syntactic, emotional and cognitive dimensions. Latent cognitive states are inferred with a Hidden Markov model. This framework opens the way to adaptive educational chatbots and conversational systems aware of the user's cognitive state.

Evolution of cognitive load, metacognition, node type and centrality over a conversation, with the inferred state sequence. Source: Cruz et al., Social Network Analysis and Mining, 2026, figure 3, CC BY 4.0 licence.

docs.text:
